title: Assessment of Quality of Life After Laparoscopic Sigma Resection with Colostomy in Paraplegic Patients
summary:
Due to a bowel dysfunction as a result of paraplegia, a laparoscopic bowel resection with a terminal bowel outlet was performed. This surgical procedure is performed to improve bowel control and increase the quality of life of affected patients.
However, the effects of this operation on the quality of life of transverse colon injury patients have not yet been sufficiently investigated. 
The aim is to assess the long-term effects of surgery on various aspects of life, including physical and mental health, social participation and daily coping with bowel outlet.

interventions.name:
Paraplegic Patients after Sigmaresection

Investigation using questionnaires: 
Assessment of health-related quality of life (HRQoL)
Patient satisfaction with the procedure
Reduction in bowel management time
Change in stool consistency
Postoperative complications
Psychological changes
Social

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Acquired paraplegia
Understanding German language
Exclusion criteria:
Congenital spinal cord lesion, neurodegenerative disease
